cards.title: FBI Probes Anti-ICE Protesters in California, Sparking Whistleblower Complaint
cards.content: The FBI opened preliminary investigations targeting anti-Immigration and Customs Enforcement protesters in Southern California, sparking a whistleblower complaint alleging violations of law and agency policy. The investigations were launched in early 2025 following demands from President Donald Trump and other administration officials. The complaint, filed by former FBI intelligence official Jill Fields, alleges that the FBI investigated and surveilled protesters without evidence of a crime, violating First Amendment protections. The Justice Department and White House have maintained that violence and obstruction of law enforcement are not protected by the First Amendment.

cards.title: France sees widespread school protests, 1,015 injured
cards.content: Hundreds of thousands of people, including high-school pupils, parents, university students, and unions, protested across France, calling for better resources for schools and less police repression. Protesters marched from the Place de la République in Paris, with clashes reported in Lyon, Paris, and Marseille. According to the government, 215 students, 85 staff, and 715 police officers were injured. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, and Education Minister Édouard Geffray appealed for dialogue. The protests have been ongoing since mid-September, with students demanding better conditions in schools.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: AMD and Intel CPUs gain traction in AI market, fueled by long-running AI agents
cards.content: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Intel are experiencing a resurgence in fortunes as their central processing units (CPUs) gain prominence in the artificial intelligence (AI) market. The companies' chips specialize in powering long-running AI agents that can work for hours on their own. AMD's growing strength in both CPUs and graphics processing units (GPUs) has pushed the company into the trillion-dollar market cap club. The CPU market is expected to reach $220 billion in sales by 2030, with AMD expecting to take more than half of the market. Intel is also seeing a surge in demand, with AMD's CPUs being favored by hyperscalers and cloud providers.

cards.title: Stock futures stable; Strait of Hormuz crisis and AI wearables concerns weigh
cards.content: Stock futures are little changed following a mixed week on Wall Street, with oil tankers in the Middle East being hit in recent days as Iran refuses to budge on its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, casting doubt on the global oil trade's recovery. Meanwhile, investors should be cautious of privacy concerns surrounding artificial intelligence-powered wearables, as major technology companies have bet on these devices to make their mark on the consumer hardware space.

cards.title: Microsoft CEO Prioritizes AI Deployment Within Enterprises
cards.content: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella emphasized the importance of "diffusion inside the enterprise" to adapt to the AI age, highlighting the need for AI tools to be widely deployed. Microsoft is trying to magnify its role in the AI boom, but faces challenges as Nvidia dominates in AI chips and Google's Gemini-powered services are popular. Nadella's AI strategy is centered around Copilot, but the company's sluggishness in keeping up with rapid changes has cost GitHub market share. Microsoft is now shifting to consumption-based pricing, with usage-based billing for Copilot Cowork, a new product. Nadella aims to empower nontechnical knowledge workers and has been downplaying the importance of world-beating models in isolation.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Pennsylvania Reports 1,000 Measles Cases, 5 Deaths, Amid Outbreak
cards.content: In the United States, a measles outbreak has been reported in Pennsylvania, with nearly 1,000 cases and five deaths. The outbreak is particularly severe in Lancaster County, where the Amish community is vulnerable to the disease. The Central Pennsylvania Clinic is at the forefront of the response, providing care to patients and raising awareness about the importance of vaccination. Clinic leaders, including Dr. Katherine Mascia, emphasize the need for consistent messaging and building trust with the community to increase vaccination rates.

cards.title: Kenya confirms first-ever Ebola case, patient dies in Nairobi
cards.content: Kenya has confirmed its first-ever Ebola case, a Kenyan citizen who died days after arriving in Nairobi. The patient, who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo, died despite being treated in several hospitals. The country has since stepped up surveillance at airports and border crossings. Over 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, with the current outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo species. The virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids, and Kenya has introduced tighter checks at airports and border posts.

cards.title: Wales sees one-third of men die prematurely, urging health plan
cards.content: A report from men's charity Movember highlights alarming statistics on men's health in Wales, where a third of men die before their 75th birthday. Ben Lidgey's personal experience, which began with a minor testicular injury, led to a cancer diagnosis and later, mental health concerns. The report urges the Welsh government to develop a dedicated plan for men's health, citing high rates of premature mortality due to preventable conditions. The Welsh economy faces annual costs of £1.4 billion from the top five causes of male premature death. Experts emphasize the importance of addressing men's reluctance to seek help for both physical and mental health issues.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Report Warns Carbon Emissions' Economic Damages Four Times Higher Than Estimated
cards.content: A new report from Future Earth, The Earth League, and the World Climate Research Programme warns that economic damages from carbon emissions could be four times higher than previously estimated. The report, 10 New Insights in Climate Science 2026/2027, finds that 2025 was 1.43°C warmer than the pre-industrial baseline, with global sea level rise already locked in for centuries. The report highlights the urgent need for climate action, as the rate of global mean sea level rise has doubled over the past 30 years, and estimates that emissions through 2050 could lock in an additional 300 millimetres of sea level rise by 2300.

cards.title: Report: Economic Damages Quadrupled, Sea Level Rise Locked In for Centuries
cards.content: A new report by Future Earth, The Earth League, and the World Climate Research Programme warns that economic damages from carbon emissions could be four times higher than previously estimated, while global sea level rise is already locked in for centuries. The report finds that 2025 was the 11th warmest year on record, with human activities releasing a record 38.1 billion tonnes of CO2. The report highlights the risks of crossing the 1.5°C threshold, with Johan Rockström stating that "the evidence is unequivocal: 1.5°C is a limit that we cross at our own risk." The report also estimates that continued climate policies could lock in an additional 600-800 millimetres of global mean sea level rise by 2300.

cards.title: Northern India faces mixed weather, rain and snow expected in some areas
cards.content: Northern India is expected to experience a mixed bag of weather conditions, with rain and snowfall forecasted in some areas. Delhi and nearby plains are expected to continue facing heat and humidity, with temperatures potentially dropping by 2-4 degrees Celsius in the coming days. Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand may receive rain, while higher mountain areas could see light snowfall. Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura are forecasted to receive heavy rain, with a yellow alert issued by the weather department. Thunderstorms, lightning, and strong winds may also affect several states, while Pilani recorded the country's highest temperature at 40.1 degrees Celsius.

sections.title: Entertainment

cards.title: Global film festivals spotlight a new generation of filmmakers
cards.content: Film festivals around the world are giving greater attention to emerging directors and independent productions. Organisers say new filmmakers are experimenting with storytelling techniques and technologies while exploring social and cultural themes.

cards.title: New stadium technology changes how fans experience live sports
cards.content: Sports venues are adopting larger digital displays, real-time statistics and connected services to create more interactive experiences for spectators. The technology is also helping teams analyse matches and improve stadium operations.

cards.title: Music platforms experiment with new ways for artists to reach audiences
cards.content: Music platforms are experimenting with new discovery tools, personalised recommendations and direct connections between artists and listeners. The changes are reshaping how new musicians build audiences and release their work.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Paramount Skydance acquires Warner Bros Discovery in $110bn merger.
cards.content: Paramount Skydance has acquired Warner Bros Discovery in a $110bn merger, reshaping Hollywood and the media landscape. The deal brings together iconic franchises like Harry Potter, Game of Thrones, and The Lord of the Rings, as well as existing Paramount hits. The merged entity, Skydance Corporation, will be led by David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz, with a focus on cost efficiencies and streaming operations. The deal has received approval from competition authorities and includes a commitment to maintain editorial independence at CNN and CBS. The merger aims to produce "real, robust movies" and create economic activity, with guardrails in place to prevent AI-generated films.

cards.title: Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros Discovery Complete $110bn Merger
cards.content: The $110bn merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros Discovery has completed, forming Skydance, an entertainment behemoth. The deal brings together franchises like Harry Potter and Game of Thrones, as well as HBO Max and Paramount+ streaming platforms. The merged company carries $80bn in debt and targets $6bn in annual cost savings. Analysts predict price increases for subscribers, with 156 movies to be released annually for five years. The merger may lead to fewer films in cinemas, with the potential for job losses and a shift towards streaming. A news editorial independence board has been established to address concerns over journalistic freedom at CNN and CBS.

cards.title: Jaguar Unveils £130,000 Electric Car, Type 01, with 1000 HP and 320-Mile Range
cards.content: Jaguar has unveiled its new electric car, the Type 01, two years after its rebranding sparked a backlash. The car, with a price tag of £130,000 in the UK, features 1000 horsepower and a range of up to 320 miles. The unveiling was met with mixed reactions, with some praising the design while others criticized it as "polarizing". Jaguar's decision to go all-electric is a gamble, given the decline of EV popularity in the US. The company faces an uphill battle, but its new strategy aims to reinvent the brand as a luxury electric marque. The future of Jaguar hangs in the balance, with some experts viewing this as a last throw of the dice.
